sources.citation: Røsok, Marie Iversdatter. 2016. /qààmîsték ʋúúrsìté/ The Sound Pattern of Aari. MA thesis, University of Oslo. 154 pp. (hdl:10852/54038; NVA record 019c94443c01-c6c1bfde-dfed-4440-8bef-805f72a4a1b8)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: RELATED VARIETY ONLY (Aari aari1239, Wubamer dialect; p.12 'my descriptions in this thesis are of the Wubamer dialect of Aari'; Galila/Gayil is named as the northern dialect but not described). Ch.5 pp.86-89: 'Hayward (1990) has suggested that Aari is an accent language. I, on the other hand, have found that Aari is a proper tone language'.. 'Aari has two tones, one high (H) and one low (L). Both the H and L tones can occur multiple times within the same word and there are no strict patterns for what syllables take what tones.' Sec.1.5.4 (pp.26-27) summarises Hayward 1990:439 (one H per word,…

sources.citation: SIL.org language page for [gyl] and SIL archives record 52540 (the Internet Archive 2015 captures)
sources.note: Index only: SIL lists just ESR 2013-007 and Alemayehu Abebe 2002 (Ometo survey II) for Gayil; no phonology/orthography statement archived online.

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda, Hussein Mohammed & Carol Magnusson. 2013. Sociolinguistic Survey of Gayil. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-007. Dallas: SIL International. 39 pp. (SIL archives entry 52540; via the Internet Archive of sil.org reapdata)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (RTT with Southern Aari texts, interviews, wordlist similarity); no phonology. Only an RTT subject's remark 'Difference between geminated and stressed words' in an appendix table (extracted text pp.36-37). Sec.1.2-1.3: Gayil = Galila = Fleming's 'Northern Ari'; notes Ford 1985 (unpublished) contains 'a brief description of Aari phonology'.

sources.note: Nothing; intelligibility and ethnolinguistic-identity arguments only.
